l4_steps.name: Extract historical MRO spend from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.input: Prior-year actuals, cost centre hierarchy, work order history
l4_steps.output: 3-year MRO spend baseline by category (line, heavy, components, engines)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS work order costs and SAP cost centres may not be fully reconciled if interface mappings were altered during AMOS upgrades, producing baseline gaps

l4_steps.name: Validate cost centre structure for MRO domains
l4_steps.input: Chart of accounts, maintenance cost centre master data
l4_steps.output: Validated cost centre tree mapped to AMOS task-card categories
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of AMOS work order types mapped to SAP cost centre before budget lock
l4_steps.pain_point: New regulatory requirements (EASA Part-145, FAR Part 145) occasionally introduce new work-scope categories with no corresponding SAP cost centre, delaying budget submission

l4_steps.name: Set annual MRO budget targets by category
l4_steps.input: Baseline spend, fleet plan, planned utilisation hours, escalation indices
l4_steps.output: Approved annual MRO budget with monthly phasing per cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Budget submission on time (T-60 days before fiscal year start)
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet utilisation assumptions from Amadeus SkyWORKS schedule plan may diverge from finance model, requiring manual reconciliation loop between Planning and Engineering

l4_steps.name: Record labour and material costs to work orders
l4_steps.input: Signed-off task cards, parts consumption records, technician time sheets
l4_steps.output: Costed work orders with labour hours, part numbers, and unit prices
l4_steps.kpi: Work order cost closure within 48 hours of task completion; <2% late-closure rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Technician time entries in AMOS depend on line-station connectivity; remote outstations with poor VPN links accumulate backlog of uncosted work orders, distorting weekly cost reports

l4_steps.name: Allocate vendor costs to work orders via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: PO line items for outsourced maintenance, AMOS work order references
l4_steps.output: Work orders with vendor cost allocations and PO cross-references
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of vendor POs linked to a work order before invoice approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Ad-hoc AOG purchases placed verbally and backed by emergency POs are frequently missing work order references, requiring retrospective allocation that delays month-end close by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Validate work order cost allocation completeness
l4_steps.input: Open and closed work orders for the reporting period
l4_steps.output: Allocation validation report; unallocated cost exception list
l4_steps.kpi: ≤1% of period spend unallocated at month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS does not enforce mandatory cost-centre fields on all work order types; engineering change orders may slip through without allocation flags

l4_steps.name: Receive and register vendor invoices in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice (PDF/EDI), purchase order number, goods receipt note
l4_steps.output: Registered invoice with PO and GRN cross-references in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice registration within 24 hours of receipt; e-invoice adoption ≥70% of MRO vendors
l4_steps.pain_point: Many smaller MRO vendors (especially AOG parts suppliers) still submit paper invoices or non-standard PDF formats; manual data entry introduces keying errors that fail automated matching

l4_steps.name: Execute 3-way match: PO vs GRN vs invoice
l4_steps.input: Registered invoice, SAP Ariba PO, AMOS goods receipt note
l4_steps.output: 3-way match result: matched, price variance, or quantity variance
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass 3-way match success rate ≥85%; invoice cycle time ≤10 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Component exchange transactions (core returns) create credit/debit timing mismatches between AMOS goods receipt and vendor invoice, routinely failing automated matching and requiring manual intervention

l4_steps.name: Validate invoice scope against approved work order
l4_steps.input: 3-way match result, approved work scope from AMOS work order
l4_steps.output: Invoice approval decision: approved, disputed, or escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice dispute rate ≤5% of total MRO invoices per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendors frequently invoice for additional scope discovered during shop visits (beyond approved estimate), and contracts that lack not-to-exceed clauses result in uncontrolled cost escalation; AMOS scope change workflow is not always enforced before additional work begins

l4_steps.name: Post approved vendor invoices in SAP AP
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice from MRO Contract Manager
l4_steps.output: Posted AP document; payment scheduled per vendor payment terms
l4_steps.kpi: On-time payment rate ≥95%; early payment discount capture ≥80% where applicable
l4_steps.pain_point: Payment terms negotiated in SAP Ariba contracts are not always replicated accurately in SAP vendor master, resulting in missed early-payment discounts and occasional late-payment penalties

l4_steps.name: Extract cost and utilisation data for KPI calculation
l4_steps.input: AMOS work order actuals, SAP cost postings, flight operations utilisation data
l4_steps.output: Consolidated MRO cost and utilisation dataset in Redshift analytics schema
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline refresh completed by Day 3 of month following reporting period
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS and SAP use different fiscal period boundaries; the one-day offset between AMOS maintenance close and SAP financial close creates period-boundary mismatches that require manual correction macros in the ETL pipeline

l4_steps.name: Calculate CPFH, cost-per-cycle and maintenance cost ratio
l4_steps.input: Consolidated cost dataset, fleet utilisation hours and cycles from Jeppesen FliteDeck
l4_steps.output: KPI scorecard: CPFH by fleet type, CPD, maintenance cost as % of total operating cost
l4_steps.kpi: CPFH variance vs budget ≤±5%; maintenance cost ratio ≤15% of total operating cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen FliteDeck flight data is updated at block-off; last-minute flight diversions or technical returns can shift utilisation hours after the KPI snapshot has been taken, requiring a restatement process

l4_steps.name: Publish KPI dashboard to Power BI for stakeholders
l4_steps.output: Published Power BI dashboard with trend lines, budget vs actual, and drill-through by vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by Day 5 of the following month; stakeholder satisfaction score ≥4/5
l4_steps.pain_point: Row-level security in Power BI requires separate maintenance when new vendor contracts are onboarded; security configuration delays occasionally result in vendors seeing each other's cost data

l4_steps.name: Review KPIs against thresholds and alert on breaches
l4_steps.input: Published KPI dashboard, approved threshold parameters
l4_steps.output: KPI status: Green / Amber / Red per metric; variance alert issued for Amber/Red items
l4_steps.kpi: All Red-threshold KPIs reviewed and actioned within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold parameters are set at contract signing and rarely reviewed; fleet age progression and inflationary pressures mean legacy thresholds become misleading benchmarks that suppress appropriate escalation

l4_steps.name: Conduct root-cause analysis for cost overruns
l4_steps.input: Variance alert, work order drill-through from Power BI, vendor invoice details
l4_steps.output: Root-cause analysis report identifying driver of overrun (scope, price, volume, mix)
l4_steps.kpi: Root-cause report issued within 10 business days of period close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS work order comments are free-text with no structured categorisation, making automated root-cause clustering difficult; analysts must manually review hundreds of work orders to isolate systemic issues

l4_steps.name: Issue corrective action plan and assign owners
l4_steps.input: Root-cause analysis report, budget variance magnitude
l4_steps.output: Corrective action plan (CAP) with owner, action, and target completion date
l4_steps.kpi: CAP issued within 5 business days of root-cause sign-off; ≥80% of CAP actions closed on time
l4_steps.pain_point: No dedicated CAP tracking module in AMOS or SAP; action tracking is managed in spreadsheets, causing loss of accountability and making it difficult to evidence closure during EASA audits

l4_steps.name: Update rolling MRO cost forecast in SAP CO
l4_steps.input: Approved CAP, revised cost assumptions, updated utilisation forecast from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Revised rolling 12-month MRO cost forecast posted in SAP Controlling
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy (latest estimate vs actual at year-end) ≤±3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Utilisation forecast from Amadeus SkyWORKS is updated weekly but SAP CO planning cycles are monthly; mid-month schedule revisions (e.g. aircraft AOG grounding) are not reflected until next month's forecast, inflating CPFH variances

l4_steps.name: Prepare monthly MRO cost report for leadership
l4_steps.input: Finalised KPI dashboard, CAP status, forecast update
l4_steps.output: Executive MRO Cost Report (PDF): actuals, budget variance, CPFH trend, top 5 vendor spend
l4_steps.kpi: Report distributed by Day 7 of following month to CFO, VP Engineering, and CEO
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual narrative writing for executive commentary is time-consuming; inconsistent framing between monthly reports reduces readability and makes period-over-period trend comparison difficult
